added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: the a-review row cites "the review.tiers key at reckon/schema/flight-defaults.yaml:68", but line 68 at the named head is the role-defaults review stanza (execution_capable, sandbox, time_budget) and the review.tiers mapping the row means opens at :122-123 with light_changed_lines and light_time_budget, so the key exists and the line a reader opens is a different stanza of the same file.

the a-sprint-is-live-while-a-crew-works-it row keeps on "the largest ledger history in the batch (17 runs)", but the committed ledger docs/state/reckon/crew.json, last updated 2026-09-26 and so visible to the reading node, carries 55 runs for a-window-paces-the-lane and 52 for a-worker-cannot-write-your-home, and the same table states 39 for an-orchestrator-cannot-forget-its-obligations at :290; seventeen is this plan's own count and is correct, the superlative is not, and the keep still stands on the row's second reason, the one remaining section that makes a busy sprint read as live.

the figure caption reads "The two fully-present plans are proposed close" and pairs that with "no kept plan's bar is full", but only a-window-paces-the-lane is fully present at 9/9 in the figure and the table; a-sprint-closes-on-completable-work, the other close, is drawn at 2/3 with its s4 counted absent as a scope-limits narrative with no deliverable, so the caption asserts one full bar more than the figure draws while the close proposal itself stands on the row's own row-level reasoning.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit 402e6769 against its parent 40d23d9b — two paths, the new evidence fragment and the new SVG under the figure topic directory, both inside the declared write paths; the fragment is authored to the sibling fragment layout its first-batch predecessor uses and the figure parses under ElementTree with literal characters only.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when requires the fraction read from code at head with a file and symbol for each counted section, the last coordinator per plan, a disposition and the keep count, and a manifest naming the head; I extracted and re-ran the record's own embedded command from the reviewed worktree at head 40d23d9b and reproduced all seventeen denominators exactly (denominator-rerun.txt), checked its citations against that head with a positive control known present and a negative control known absent (citations-check.txt), re-derived the last coordinator per plan and both live marks from the committed ledger and the live pointers and they agree on all seventeen rows, verified the absence claims for a-worker-reuses-before-it-writes and a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk s4 with working controls, and checked the figure's seventeen bar widths and colours against the row fractions, which match exactly (presence.svg).
item_verdicts.goal: the reviewed node's goal is a read-only triage of seventeen pending reckon plans; the landed record docs/evidence/fragments/open-work-is-capped/triage-pending-plans-second-batch.html carries one row per plan with a presence fraction, the section-by-section citation behind it, the last coordinator marked live where a run is in flight, a proposed disposition and a one-line reason, and closes the arithmetic at keep 6, merge 9, close 2 — which matches the six keep rows, nine merge rows and two close rows I counted in the table.
item_verdicts.manifest: read in full; it reads status complete, names the reading head 40d23d9b in evidence_inputs, and names no suite because the node produces a record rather than a code change, so its baseline_suite and after_suite are legitimately empty and the added-failure count is unmeasured rather than zero.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed manifest declares docs/evidence/fragments/open-work-is-capped/triage-pending-plans-second-batch.html and docs/figures/open-work-is-capped/triage-pending-plans-second-batch, and commit 402e6769 touches exactly those two paths with no plan file edited, so both the declared scope and the read-only fence hold.

justifications.durability: nothing would fail if a future denominator or a bar drifted — no gate asserts the record's claims, the reproduction command is a manual check a reader must choose to run, and a caption that already contradicts its own figure is the defect class a gate would catch — but the record does embed that command and the figure and the rows agree bar for bar today, which is more than the first batch's record could show.
justifications.evidence: the record's embedded command reproduces all seventeen of seventeen denominators exactly, every citation I sampled resolves at the named head 40d23d9b, the two live marks and the coordinators match the committed ledger and the live pointers, and the absence claims hold with controls; against that, three prose claims do not survive their own instruments — a wrong line at :126, a false superlative at :168 and a caption at :101 that asserts a full bar the figure does not draw — and the phrase "main head" at :16 names the run's own read revision, true of its base but not of the branch at the time the figure was drawn.
justifications.fit: the fragment uses the plan-verifies, plan-artifacts and plan-verdict meta grammar its siblings use and they resolve, the figure is embedded with a project-absolute src and parses, and the commit carries a conventional subject and a body.
justifications.goal_fidelity: every one of the seventeen rows carries the required shape and the two counts I re-derived independently — the keep/merge/close arithmetic and all seventeen denominators — are correct, but one keep reason overstates its evidence at :168, claiming the largest ledger history in the batch for a plan whose seventeen runs trail three peers in the same table.
justifications.scope_discipline: commit 402e6769 changes only docs/evidence/fragments/open-work-is-capped/triage-pending-plans-second-batch.html and docs/figures/open-work-is-capped/triage-pending-plans-second-batch/presence.svg, both inside the manifest's declared paths, the worktree is clean, and no plan, ledger or index file is touched.
